title: Agent Recall
description: Makes past agent sessions searchable and points each result back to the original work, so useful context is easier to trust and reuse.
seoTitle: Agent Recall Project | Local AI Agent Memory Infrastructure
seoDescription: How an open-source local tool makes agent transcripts searchable and points every result back to its source.

relatedLinks.label: See how remote replies stay behind local approval.

constraints: Agent transcripts can contain sensitive project context, so raw archives needed to remain local and stay the source of truth.
Search results and memory records had to point back to source files and line numbers instead of becoming unverifiable summaries.
problem: Useful decisions, blockers, commands, and implementation details were scattered across local agent session archives.
Plain text search over the transcript files was too noisy. Treating those files as the database would also make recall brittle and hard to inspect.
solution: Built a Rust command-line tool that reads supported transcript archives, removes common secret patterns, keeps useful events, and adds them to a disposable local search index.
Added search, recent views, pinned references, structured memories, related context, change tracking, health checks, statistics, and structured output for other agent workflows.
Added a background watcher for macOS with freshness reporting, project and date filters, temporary-lock handling, and an optional importer for archived Codex logs.
result: Shipped a public, installable tool for local recall across Codex, OMP, Pi, Claude, and optional archived Codex log sources.
Made retrieval auditable: search results group by session and include source labels, event kinds, file paths, and exact line receipts.
Covered the risky paths with command-line, ranking, secret-removal, importing, memory extraction, watcher, and background-service tests so the tool can change without quietly breaking recall quality.
